preamble: Primary (Immune/Genetic) FSGS  |  100-Point Adverse Prognostic Score  |  KDIGO 2021 Glomerular Disease Guidelines / NephCure FSGS Guidelines  |  Progression Trajectory: Fast / Moderate / Slow

questions.question: Is the patient steroid-resistant (no remission after ≥4 weeks of adequate prednisone dose)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — steroid-resistant primary FSGS confirmed; requires second-line immunosuppression; highest ESRD risk subgroup

questions.question: Is proteinuria >3.0 g/day (PCR >3.0) despite ≥3 months of combined immunosuppression (CNI + MMF or rituximab)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — refractory nephrotic-range proteinuria on maximal immunosuppression; poor prognosis confirmed

questions.question: Has the patient achieved only partial remission (proteinuria reduced but PCR still 0.3–3.0 mg/mg) on current therapy?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — partial remission; some protection against ESRD but residual progression risk remains; optimize therapy

questions.question: Is eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73m² (CKD Stage 4) or has the patient reached ESRD requiring dialysis?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — severely reduced eGFR or ESRD; primary FSGS with steroid resistance has 50% ESRD rate within 10 years

questions.question: Is annualized eGFR decline >5 mL/min/1.73m²/year confirmed on serial measurements?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — rapid progressive CKD confirmed; ESRD trajectory without treatment change

questions.question: Is the FSGS variant collapsing on biopsy? (worst prognosis; strongly associated with APOL1 high-risk genotype or HIV)
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — collapsing FSGS confirmed; 50–70% ESRD within 3 years; APOL1 genotyping mandatory if not done

questions.question: Is there significant tubular atrophy or interstitial fibrosis (>25% of cortex) on biopsy?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — chronic irreversible nephron loss confirmed; limits expected treatment response

questions.question: Is >25% of glomeruli globally sclerosed on light microscopy?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — advanced glomerular dropout confirmed; reduced therapeutic target mass

questions.question: Are two APOL1 high-risk alleles confirmed (G1/G1, G1/G2, or G2/G2) in a patient of African ancestry?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — APOL1 high-risk genotype; doubles ESRD risk above baseline primary FSGS; collapsing variant expected

questions.question: Is there a pathogenic variant in NPHS2 (podocin) or WT1 — genes associated with rapidly progressive steroid-resistant disease?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — high-risk podocyte gene mutation confirmed; nearly universal steroid resistance; early transplant planning indicated

questions.question: Is BP persistently >140/90 mmHg despite ≥3 antihypertensives including maximum-dose RAS blockade?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — refractory hypertension on maximal therapy; major ESRD accelerator in primary FSGS

questions.question: Is there a history of venous thromboembolism (DVT, PE, or renal vein thrombosis) related to nephrotic syndrome?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — nephrotic-related thrombosis confirmed; full anticoagulation required; indicates severe hypoalbuminemia

questions.question: Has the patient had ≥1 serious infection (pneumococcal peritonitis, cellulitis, sepsis) related to immunosuppression or hypoalbuminemia?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — serious immunosuppression- or nephrotic-related infection confirmed; risk-benefit of continued treatment requires reassessment
